To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Prednisone treatment in patients with tuberculosis and HIV infection who have low CD4 cell counts reduced the incidence of tuberculosis‐related immune reconstitution inflammatory syndromes without evidence of an excess of severe infections or cancer.
prednisone treatment of patients with tuberculosis and HIV infection who were initiating ART resulted in a lower rate of tuberculosis‐associated paradoxical IRIS than placebo.
prednisone prophylaxis reduced the incidence of tuberculosis- associated IRIS in patients initiating ART, without increasing the risk of severe infections.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of glucocorticoids for the prevention of paradoxical tuberculosis-associated IRIS.
the study of the role of prednisone in the prevention of paradoxical tuberculosis associated with immune reconstitution inflammatory disease in HIV infected patients.
the development of new and improved treatment strategies for tuberculosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prednisone is a safe and effective prophylaxis against the development of tuberculosis-associated IRIS in patients with low CD-4 counts.
prednisone treatment of HIV-infected patients who are starting antiretrovials and have tuberculosis is associated with a lower incidence of paradoxical immune reconstitution inflammatory disease.
prednisone treatment during ART initiation is associated with a lower risk of paradoxical TB-IRIS, but it does not reduce the risk of severe infections and does not increase the risk of cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of prednisone in the first 4 to 6 weeks of antiretrovirals for patients with low CD-4 counts and active tuberculosis reduces the incidence of paradoxal tuberculosis-associated IRIS.
prednisone prophylaxis for 4 weeks after initiation of ART in HIV-infected patients with tuberculosis reduces the risk of paradoxal IRIS.

prednisone is safe and effective in reducing the incidence of paradoxal tuberculosis associated immune reconstitution inflammatory disease in patients with HIV and tuberculosis who are starting antiretrovial therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have a treatment that can be used in a very safe and effective way to reduce the risk of paradoxically worsening tuberculosis when starting HIV treatment.
we now have a tool for reducing paradoxical TB IRIS, and we should use it.
we can now offer a safe and effective treatment for this condition.
